history.new: For any finite set E of laws, the anchored affine tables are exactly x*y = x + a*y + 1, and the affine spectrum Aff(E) is the set of N for which the affine system of E (polynomials in Z[a]) has a common root mod N. Aff(E) is closed under divisors and under coprime products; if the system has no common factor over Q it is finite and equal to the set of divisors of its maximum L (L divides every non-zero integer of the ideal generated by the system in Z[a], e.g. any non-zero constant of the system or any non-zero resultant of two of its polynomials), and otherwise it is infinite (an empty system gives Aff(E) = N).

history.new: Elementary consequences of the CRT and of classical facts on polynomial congruences; the reduction of identities to conditions on affine (linear) representations is standard for quasigroups and medial magmas (Toyoda-Bruck). Recorded as the lab's tool, not as new mathematics. The Equational Theories Project also studies spectra of single magma laws with linear models x * y = ax + by mod n (Bolan et al., arXiv:2512.07087; noted by the Skeptic from the abstract page).
